subject: Tenant guardrails & invite plan - NeonHealth kickoff
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@neonhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NeonHealth - initial tenant setup & keys

Hi Tessa / Monica,

Thanks for getting this kicked off. We want to move from PoC to first-prod tenant for NeonHealth (scope: secure inference for clinician-facing notes). High level asks:
- Isolated tenant per org with admin roles for our security and infra teams
- API keys for service account and a small set of user invites (10 initial seats)
- Audit logs + retention policy for 90 days

Target timeline: provision tenant and seed admin keys this week, invite users early next week. Our technical contacts: Raj Patel (infra) and me (product).

Questions for you: do you recommend inviting users via Redwood-managed invites or should we wire up SSO from day one? Also want to confirm approach for API key rotation & ephemeral service tokens.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
Head of Product, NeonHealth

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@neonhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@neonhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonHealth - initial tenant setup & keys

Hi Sara — great to meet you (virtually). Monica and I will own the CS handoff + invite cadence; Jonas will handle the implementation details. Proposed lightweight plan to get you into a secure tenant this week:

1) Create NeonHealth project namespace + admin group (owners: sara.lim@neonhealth.com, raj.patel@neonhealth.com)
2) Seed two admin API keys (one long-lived for ops, one rotated for CI) and provision an ephemeral service account for nightly jobs
3) Create roles: admin, developer, viewer — map initial 10 invites to developer/viewer as needed
4) Enable audit logging and set 90-day retention in the tenant settings
5) Run a canary deployment for token exchange to validate cache/KV handling before inviting end users

Attachments I'm sending: an invite-email template and a milestone tracker (spreadsheet) that outlines owners and ETA. Quick question — if you plan to onboard via SSO, we can hold on invites; otherwise we will send Redwood-managed invites tomorrow. Which do you prefer?

Next steps: please confirm SSO status and the two people who should be in the initial admin group.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@neonhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonHealth - initial tenant setup & keys

Thanks Tessa — quick reply. SSO (Okta) integration isn't going to be ready this week; we'll likely have Okta live in ~3 weeks. For initial rollout, please proceed with Redwood-managed invites + a service account for our ingestion pipeline.

A couple of technical constraints:
- Service account keys must be revocable by our ops (is there a way to tag keys then revoke from the console?)
- We prefer token TTL no longer than 24h for service jobs; long-lived keys only for manual admin operations

Sounds like the plan you outlined works. Please populate the milestone sheet with proposed dates and owners and we'll confirm.

— Raj
Infrastructure Lead, NeonHealth

Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonHealth - initial tenant setup & keys

Hi all — technical follow-up and recommended defaults from the infra side:

- Service account & keys: we'll create a service account with scoped permissions ("ingest:write", "models:call"). Keys will be labeled (metadata) so Neon ops can identify them; keys can be revoked via the Redwood Console under Tenant -> Keys.
- Token TTL: default 24h for ephemeral tokens; we can issue refresh tokens for CI with a 7-day TTL if you need longer-lived exchange flows.
- API key rotation: we'll provide a rotation script that hits the Keys API and swaps keys with zero downtime if you adopt the canary path.
- Audit logs: logs are exported to the tenant S3 bucket by default; retention set to 90 days as requested. We can increase to 180 if you need for compliance.

Action items I will take today:
- Provision NeonHealth namespace and seed the two admin keys (ops + CI)
- Upload milestone tracker to shared doc and flag the canary window (we recommend nightly low-traffic window 02:00-04:00 PT)

[Attachment: neon_implementation_milestones.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

If Sara/Raj confirm Redwood-managed invites, we'll seed the developer invites tomorrow morning.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
